items.t: The page's structure as read: a six-bullet "short version," an eight-step "How selling works, step by step" sequence, a "What it costs to sell a home in B.C." section, a home-value lead form ("What is your home worth?"), a "Why work with me" block, and six seller questions with answers, with a link onward to a seller FAQ page.

The page's stated starting point: a free, no-pressure chat about goals and timing; pricing based on what similar homes nearby have recently sold for; Jared handling photos, the MLS® listing, showings and offers; and written disclosures under BC rules walked through with the seller.

Where condo stock concentrates for this page: the page names no stock at all — it is a process page whose housing references are the seller's own home, whatever its type; a South Surrey or Langley condo seller uses the same eight steps, and the condo-specific diligence in a sale (strata documents a buyer will request) is governed by the Form B regime in, not by anything this page states about stock.

items.t: Commission on this page: the page states no commission rate, amount or structure anywhere, so what a seller pays Jared's brokerage is not verified from this page — under the BCFSA framework above, commission and fee information is given to the consumer in the listing conversation, off-page.

Deposits generally (BCFSA): a buyer's deposit is usually held in the brokerage's trust account with the brokerage as stakeholder, a neutral party; where subject clauses are not removed, the deposit is not automatically returned and both parties must sign a release, except where the buyer exercises the right of rescission.

BC home flipping tax, verified on the Province page the selling page links to: the tax applies to profit from selling a BC property (including presale contracts) owned for less than 730 days, under the Residential Property (Short-Term Holding) Profit Tax Act effective January 1, 2025; the rate is 20% of net taxable income for a property disposed of within 365 days and gradually decreases over the next 365 days, with no tax at 730 days; a return must be filed within 90 days of the sale where the seller is subject to the tax or an exemption applies only after filing. The page's shorter wording — "20% of the profit," "drops to zero by day 730," "a return may be due within 90 days" — is a simplification of "net taxable income" and the filing conditions as the Province states them.

blocks.text: Good to know about Selling

items.t: The page's costs list omits the largest cost of selling.

Two pages of the same site promise different marketing deliverables. This page states twice that "Staging help, professional video, floor plans and drone photos come with every listing," while the site's marketing-plan page names photography, online exposure, digital/social promotion and listing materials but does not name video, drone or floor plans at all — whether every listing in fact receives all four items is a practice claim that cannot be confirmed from either page: Not verified.
The home-value form is a black box in the text read.

The page's flipping-tax wording is a simplification of the Province's. Where the page says "20% of the profit," the Province's own page — the one the selling page links to — says 20% of net taxable income within 365 days, gradually decreasing over the next 365 days, with the filing conditions stated in full; a seller pricing a quick sale off the page's short version alone would understate the detail that decides the bill.

The rescission fee reaches the seller without a release form — a detail sellers rarely know in advance. BCFSA states that on a rescission within three business days the brokerage pays the seller the 0.25% fee directly and returns the balance of the deposit to the buyer, with no separate release form signed by either party — unlike a subject-removal failure, where both parties must sign a release before any deposit moves.
This selling page's scope is deliberately narrow.
The typical reader is deciding whether to list, not yet listing.

items.t: The largest cost of selling is the one the costs section never mentions. Commission is the cost BCFSA's consumer framework leads with, and this page's BCFSA-attributed list omits it entirely — a seller budgeting from the page alone under-budgets by the biggest line.
The ranking line does double duty and double exposure.

A process page still carries strata law. Nothing on the selling page mentions the Form B, void rental bylaws or the 55+ bylaw rule — yet for a strata townhome seller those three rules decide what a buyer can diligence, what can be marketed, and who can buy.

items.t: Land as the page treats it — process only: the page's eight steps (first chat; pricing from recent nearby sales and current listings; getting ready; photos and listing; showings; offers; conditions and cooling-off; closing) are written for a home seller and are stated by the page without any lot-specific step — no servicing, subdivision, ALR or buildability step appears in the page's process.

The costs section as the page states it (site copy, attributed on the page to BCFSA): legal or notary fees for the title transfer; legal fees to discharge the mortgage; GST on legal fees; any prepayment penalty from the lender; and the seller's share of the current year's property taxes if not already paid — with advice to talk to an accountant for tax questions.
The selling page does not distinguish bare-land strata lots from built homes anywhere in its text: no bare-land strata treatment is documented by this page.
Tenure default: fee-simple is the default for a resale lot; the page states no tenure position for land, and none is asserted for it here.
Assemblies / proposals: none is named, described or carried by this page, and none is documented here as inventory.

items.t: : the page states no commission rate, amount or structure anywhere, and its BCFSA-attributed costs list omits commission entirely, even though commission is the cost BCFSA's consumer framework leads with. What a seller pays Jared's brokerage is therefore not verified from this page — under the BCFSA framework above, commission and fee information is given to the consumer in the listing conversation, off-page.

Cooling-off / rescission, verified at the regulator: if a buyer rescinds an accepted offer under the Home Buyer Rescission Period Regulation within three business days, the brokerage pays the seller the 0.25% rescission fee directly and returns the remaining balance of the deposit to the buyer, with no separate release form signed by either party. Deposits generally: a buyer's deposit is usually held in the brokerage's trust account with the brokerage as stakeholder; where subject clauses are not removed, the deposit is not automatically returned and both parties must sign a release, except where the buyer exercises the right of rescission.

Municipal frames for a land seller (kept separate — the page spans both cities): Surrey ground — OCP Bylaw No. 21900 (adopted June 15, 2026; Bylaw 18020 is REPLACED, never cited as current), Zoning Bylaw No. 12000, suite cap 40% of principal habitable area, subdivision/servicing under Bylaw 8830 (1986), verified on City pages. Township of Langley ground — Zoning Bylaw 2500, SSMUH Bylaw 6020 (NO 6-plex tier), suite cap 120 m², coach house fee-simple under s.102 (never strata), Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw 2019 No. 5382 CONFIRMED. Langley City ground — Zoning 2025 No. 3300 by number (adoption date not verified), SSMUH Bylaw 3284, suite = lesser of 100 m² and 40%. Which frame governs a lot sale depends on the parcel's own municipality; the selling page states none of this and no frame is asserted for the page itself.

Strata block (a bare-land strata lot sale, where one exists): Form B within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2 + May 1, 2023 exemptions). A "45+" listing line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw. A fee-simple lot carries none of this.

PTT — worked example (inputs + tier math; a buyer's tax, stated here because sellers price against it): on a $900,000 lot purchase — 1% on the first $200,000 ($2,000) + 2% on $200,000–$900,000 ($14,000) = $16,000. Tiers: 1% to $200,000, 2% to $2,000,000, 3% above, plus a further 2% on the residential portion over $3,000,000.

REDMA note (presale contracts only): a presale sale is not this page's process — REDMA s.21 gives a purchaser a 7-day rescission right and s.18 requires deposits in trust; carried here only so a presale seller is not priced off this page's resale steps.

items.t: The largest selling cost is the one the page never mentions. The costs section's BCFSA-attributed list covers legal/notary fees, mortgage discharge, GST on legal fees, a possible prepayment penalty and property-tax share — and omits commission entirely, so a seller budgeting from the page alone misses the biggest line.

The cooling-off fee needs no release form. Where a buyer rescinds inside three business days, the brokerage pays the seller the 0.25% fee directly from the deposit and returns the balance to the buyer — no separate release signed by either party — unlike a failed subject removal, where both parties must sign a release before any deposit moves.

The flipping tax is on net taxable income, not "profit" in the page's shorthand. The Province's rate is 20% of net taxable income inside 365 days, grading to zero at day 730, and a return can be due within 90 days even where an exemption applies only after filing — the page's shorter wording simplifies both points.
The sell-my-house-fast page does NOT document the claim wording in (a) — it is never imported there, and nothing documented only for that page is asserted here.

Approved claims, as page statements only: REALTOR since 2015 (stated on the page and matching); 10 straight years FVREB Medallion Club; Top 1%; #1 in South Surrey/White Rock by MLS points 2025 + 2026 YTD; $500M+ sales.
